title: Symphony No. 5 in D minor
hook: A triumphant ending, or the sound of being forced to cheer? You decide.

painting.title: Torso in a Yellow Shirt (Complicated Premonition)
painting.pairingNote: A faceless figure in an empty landscape, painted in the same country and decade, by an artist who was also under official pressure.

facts: In January 1936 the newspaper Pravda attacked Shostakovich’s music in an article headed “Muddle Instead of Music”. In Stalin’s Soviet Union, that put his career and his life in danger.
He wrote the Fifth Symphony between April and July 1937, at the height of the Great Terror.
The premiere, on 21 November 1937 in Leningrad under Evgeny Mravinsky, was a sensation. People wept during the slow movement, and the ovation reportedly lasted half an hour.
The symphony restored Shostakovich to official favour. Listeners have argued ever since about what its triumphant ending really means.
bigPicture.inOneLine: questioning (I), sarcasm (II), mourning (III), triumph in quotation marks (IV).

movements.heading: Moderato
movements.summary: A slow-burning [[sonata-form|sonata form]] movement. Two quiet, cold themes are gradually seized by the brass and drums and turned into a brutal march.

mainIdeas.name: The opening gesture
mainIdeas.description: jagged leaps, low strings answered by high strings.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a quiet, winding melody in the violins that keeps sinking.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: very long, widely spaced notes in the violins, floating over a soft repeating rhythm (long, short-short).

stops.hear: Low strings leap upward; high strings answer a moment later with the same shape
stops.happening: The opening gesture, in [[canon|canon]]

stops.hear: A quiet, drooping melody in the violins
stops.happening: Theme 1

stops.hear: The music becomes very still: long, high violin notes over a gently pulsing accompaniment
stops.happening: Theme 2. Calm, but icy

stops.hear: A piano enters, low and percussive; horns growl out Theme 1
stops.happening: The [[development|development]]. The tempo starts to accelerate

stops.hear: Trumpets and a snare drum: Theme 1 as a strutting march
stops.happening: The lyrical melody has become grotesque

stops.hear: The whole orchestra, in [[unison|unison]], hurls out the opening gesture; a gong crashes
stops.happening: The climax, which is also the start of the [[recapitulation|recapitulation]]

stops.hear: A flute and a horn sing Theme 2 to each other, one a step behind the other
stops.happening: Theme 2 in D major, in gentle [[canon|canon]]. The most tender moment in the movement

stops.label: Last 90 seconds
stops.hear: A solo violin, then rising, glassy notes from the celesta
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]]. The movement ends with a question, not an answer

notice: The march at ≈ 10:00 uses exactly the same notes as the quiet Theme 1. The transformation is the message.

movements.heading: Allegretto
movements.summary: A short, heavy-footed [[scherzo|scherzo]] in waltz time. The humour has an edge.

stops.hear: Cellos and basses begin gruffly, alone
stops.happening: A clumsy, stamping start

stops.hear: A shrill small clarinet, then pompous horns
stops.happening: A parade of caricatures, in the manner of a [[landler|Ländler]]

stops.hear: A solo violin plays a coy little tune with slides, over harp
stops.happening: The [[trio|trio]]. A flute repeats it. The [[glissando|glissando]] slides make it sound mock-innocent

stops.hear: The opening returns, now tiptoeing: bassoon and plucked strings
stops.happening: The scherzo comes back in [[pizzicato|pizzicato]]

stops.label: Last 20 seconds
stops.hear: The oboe recalls the coy tune, now in the minor; then a loud dismissal
stops.happening: A sour afterthought

movements.heading: Largo
movements.summary: The heart of the symphony, and the movement that made the first audience weep. The brass are silent throughout. The strings are divided into eight separate parts.

stops.hear: Violins alone, quiet and hymn-like; other strings join one group at a time
stops.happening: The first theme. The strings play [[divisi|divisi]], building a choir-like texture

stops.hear: A flute and harp, almost alone
stops.happening: A lonely second melody

stops.hear: A solo oboe over a single thread of trembling violins
stops.happening: The most desolate passage. Clarinet and flute follow, each alone

stops.hear: The cellos cry out at the top of their range; a xylophone hammers; double basses grind beneath
stops.happening: The climax. Grief breaks into the open

stops.hear: The music subsides to a whisper
stops.happening: The aftermath

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: Harp and celesta pick out the lonely melody, note by note; a soft major chord
stops.happening: An ending of exhausted peace

notice: There is no brass in this movement. After the marches of the first movement, their silence is felt.

movements.heading: Allegro non troppo
movements.summary: Drums and brass burst in with a march. After a quiet, reflective middle, the march returns and builds to a blazing D major. Whether that ending is a victory is the question the symphony leaves open.

stops.hear: Pounding timpani; trumpets and trombones blare out a march
stops.happening: Theme 1. It gets faster and faster

stops.hear: A solo trumpet sings a broad new melody over swirling strings
stops.happening: Theme 2. It rises to a climax, then collapses

stops.hear: Quiet. A solo horn plays the trumpet’s melody, gently
stops.happening: The reflective middle section

stops.hear: Violins rock back and forth over harp notes
stops.happening: Shostakovich quotes one of his own songs here, a setting of a Pushkin poem called “Rebirth”

stops.hear: A snare drum taps softly; woodwinds bring back the march, slowly
stops.happening: The long build to the ending begins

stops.label: Last 90 seconds
stops.hear: The brass proclaim the march theme in D major while the strings hammer one single note, over and over
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]]. The strings repeat the same note more than two hundred times

stops.label: Last bars
stops.hear: Timpani and bass drum pound out the final notes
stops.happening: The end

notice: Listen to the strings in the final minute, not the brass. That one hammered note can sound like rejoicing or like being beaten.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Bernstein takes the ending fast, and it sounds like a real triumph. Many conductors, including Mravinsky, play it at about half that speed, and then it sounds heavy and forced. Compare the two; the difference is the whole debate in miniature.

threads.title: Themes turned into marches
threads.body: Quiet melodies are repeatedly taken over by brass and drums.

threads.title: The missing brass
threads.body: Their silence in the Largo is as expressive as their noise elsewhere.

threads.title: The open question
threads.body: The symphony gives the authorities a triumphant finale and gives listeners room to doubt it.
